column1: # Each row IS a gate decision point. The generator scores a firing by walking the rows whose
# milestone matches and taking the first whose ERE matches the recorded reason; a reason no row
# matches is a HARD FAILURE naming the record, never an `other` bucket (#609 D-c). A row that
# never matches anything is not dead weight — it is how a point that has never fired still gets
# enumerated with a count of zero, which is most of what the report has to say.
# Columns: gate_point <TAB> milestone <TAB> obligation <TAB> ERE over the reason <TAB> label
# `obligation` is "-" where the gate writes no obligation row for the point.
# `earn_your_keep` (#641) names the regression class this point ALONE catches — the class no
# other row in this table, and no other gate, already accounts for — and cites a dated incident
# where one exists. gate-ablation.awk reads only the first five columns; this one is read by a
# human deciding whether a point still earns its refusal, the same discipline
# docs/testing.md's earn-your-keep rule applies to mutation-catalog.tsv rows.
# Order is significant WITHIN a milestone (first match wins) and is the render order of the
# decision-points table. Patterns are anchored where the gate message is anchored.

column5: the run has not written its spec yet
column6: a build session that skips straight to implementation with no spec on the branch at all — the one point that catches "no spec was ever written", distinct from every m1 row below it, which all assume a spec exists and score its contents

column5: the spec declares no AC-n
column6: a spec with prose but no enumerable, individually-satisfiable AC-n set, which would leave milestone 3's later gate with nothing concrete to check the build against

column5: the spec's Decision Ledger is malformed
column6: a Decision Ledger row whose provenance is outside the enum (e.g. 'assumed'), which is the specific defect ledger-lint.sh exists to catch — a build session asserting a decision was made without saying by whom

column4: does not reconcile with the pre-flight ledger
column5: the spec drops or re-decides a bound receipt row
column6: a build session silently re-deciding a question the pre-flight interview already resolved, instead of carrying the ratified answer forward or filing a DEPARTURE row against it

column5: an Open Region needs an operator answer first
column6: a build session proceeding past a spec region the intake interview explicitly marked as requiring a human answer before implementation starts

column5: the spec's Design section is neither armed nor disarmed
column6: a spec that leaves Design ambiguous — neither a disarm reason nor an armed handoff with RS-n rows — which would leave milestone 3's design-render check unable to tell whether it should run at all

column5: the PR edits a release-owned file
column6: a feature PR bumping plugin.json version or hand-editing CHANGELOG.md — release artifacts this repo's own CLAUDE.md derives at release time only (retired by #119); the one point standing between that convention and a red PR

column5: a plugins PR carries no Changelog trailer
column6: a plugins/** PR with neither a Changelog: trailer nor a Changelog: none, which would leave the release notes assembler with nothing to read for that change — the only mechanical enforcement of CLAUDE.md's trailer convention

column5: the configured lint lane is red
column6: a shell syntax or shellcheck defect landing on the branch — the only point that runs the repo's configured lint command at all before merge

column5: the configured typecheck lane is red
column6: a type error in a consumer repo that configures a typecheck lane; this repo's own config leaves typecheck null, so this row fires only for consumers, never for second-shift's own dogfood runs

column5: the configured test lane is red
column6: a behavioral regression in the tree — the only point that runs the configured test command (this repo's selftest sweep) before merge; without it a build could ship a red suite straight to review

column5: a configured extra verifying lane is red
column6: a mutation-sweep survivor or other configured extra lane going red mid-build — catches what the primary test lane's pass/fail alone cannot: a suite that passes but would not have caught the mutant it was paired against

column5: a configured setup lane is red or malformed
column6: a repo's own lane configuration being unreadable or its setup step failing, which is an infra defect distinct from every other m3 row's "the code is wrong" — this is "the check itself could not run"

column5: the repo configures nothing that verifies
column6: a consumer repo whose config wires no test/lint/typecheck lane at all, which would let milestone 3 pass vacuously with nothing evaluated — the one row that catches an EMPTY verification contract, not a failing one

column5: the armed design render lane could not produce a receipt
column6: an armed ticket (design.provider configured, RS-n rows present) whose render step fails to produce the hashed receipt milestone 3 blocks on — catches a design-fidelity claim with nothing behind it, distinct from m1/design-form's "the section is missing" check

column5: the review has not been handed off yet
column6: a build session attempting to close out before any review session has ever run — the base case every other m4 row assumes past

column5: the review returned needs-work
column6: the ordinary review-round loop: a needs-work verdict with real blockers, which is the point converting review findings into a build obligation rather than an advisory comment

column5: the verdict record is missing a required header key
column6: a malformed verdict record missing a key the merge boundary's reconciliation depends on — an infra defect in the record itself, not a review finding about the code

column4: (exists but was never committed|has uncommitted changes)
column5: the verdict record is not on the branch
column6: a verdict record that exists on disk in a review session's worktree but was never actually committed — catches "the review ran but its evidence never landed", which no CI check on the PR branch alone could see

column4: (carries the BUILD run's identity|names the BUILD session)
column5: the build session authored its own verdict
column6: a build session writing (or being credited with) its own approve verdict — the mechanical enforcement of P10: generation and evaluation run in separate contexts. #348 deleted the in-build reviewer and the dispatch-failure fallback that used to make this reachable; this row is what stays refusing it now that the fallback is gone

column5: the round chain does not reach back to a committed record
column6: a multi-round review (r2, r3, ...) whose inherited_patch_id does not chain back to the prior round's record — catches a broken round history, distinct from m4/patch-stale's "the same round's patch moved"

column4: (file\(s\) changed after it|now hashes to|own diff has moved since)
column5: content moved after the review
column6: a commit pushed after an approve verdict was recorded — the exact shape #372 named: a rebase that replays the branch unchanged does not re-stamp, but new content does, and this row is the only thing distinguishing the two

column4: is not a commit in this branch's history
column5: the reviewed commit no longer exists on the branch
column6: a force-push or rebase that dropped the exact commit a verdict was recorded against — an integrity failure distinct from ordinary content drift, since there is no diff to even compare

column4: differ between that commit and the current head
column5: the review read a different tree
column6: the reviewed commit exists on the branch but a merge or rebase changed what tree it resolves to — catches divergence a bare sha-existence check (m4/head-missing) would miss

column5: an armed ticket's design fidelity is unscored or stale
column6: an armed ticket (RS-n rows present) whose design fidelity score is missing or does not match the reviewed patch — the design-receipt analogue of m4/patch-stale, scoped to the rendered-UI claim rather than the code diff

column5: an earlier milestone left no satisfied record
column6: a close-out attempted while an earlier milestone's own record is stale relative to the current tree — catches "milestone 4 passed, then the branch moved, and nothing re-ran 2/3" before close-out compounds the gap

column4: ^(no open PR found for branch|could not list PRs for)
column5: no open PR for the lane branch
column6: a close-out attempted with no open PR at all — the PR the whole lane exists to produce is simply missing, distinct from every other m5/exit-artifacts row, which assume a PR exists and check its shape

column5: the PR is still a draft
column6: a draft PR reaching close-out — catches an unready PR a reviewer was never meant to see merged, since a draft raises no pull_request event a merge-gating CI run would act on

column5: the PR body does not close the issue
column6: a PR whose body never links back to its issue via a Closes trailer — without this row the issue tracker would never auto-close on merge, silently reopening the same ticket next triage pass

column4: does not link the committed spec
column5: the PR body does not link the spec
column6: a PR body omitting the link to docs/plans/<key>-lean.md — catches "a reviewer has to go find the spec themselves", the one artifact-chain link P1 names explicitly

column4: ^(no closing comment on|could not fetch the comment trail)
column5: no closing comment references the verdict record
column6: a close-out that never posted the one tracker-visible pointer from the issue back to the committed verdict record — without it, an auditor reading the issue thread has no path to the evidence that gated the merge

column4: does not reference the verdict record
column5: the PR body does not reference the verdict record
column6: the PR-body twin of the closing-comment row above, scoped to readers who never open the issue at all — a PR-only auditor with no path to the verdict record without this row

column5: the PR carries no build identity marker
column6: a PR whose bot-authored identity marker never landed — the marker milestone 4's boundary check compares the verdict's authored-by identity against; without it, m4/identity has nothing on the PR side to reconcile against
